evals.prompt: I've got the stackoverflow OKF bundle checked out in ./stackoverflow. Is it valid OKF 0.2? And which concepts would you not trust for a metrics dashboard and why?
evals.expected_output: Conformance verdict with counts; points out the numbered [^1] footnotes that don't key into sources ids; lists concepts by trust tier / status / staleness with reasons.
assertions: Response gives an explicit conformance verdict that the bundle is valid/conformant OKF 0.2 (no hard errors)
Response flags the numbered [^1] footnotes that do not key into sources[].id (posts_questions / votes)
Response notes that every concept is unverified (no `verified` field anywhere)
Response flags tables/stackoverflow_posts as deprecated and not to be used
Response notes the metrics are not Attested Computations (no sanctioned computation / runtime / attester)
Bundle files were left unmodified

evals.prompt: add a concept to the acme_retail bundle for our new bigquery table acme.sales.returns - columns return_id STRING, order_id STRING (fk to orders), refund_usd NUMERIC, returned_at TIMESTAMP. i wrote the ddl myself, its documented at https://wiki.acme/data/returns. update whatever else needs updating
evals.expected_output: New tables/returns.md with type, title, description, resource, generated by the agent (not human), no fabricated verified, sources entry with id and footnote, schema table, bundle-relative link to orders; tables/index.md and log.md updated; bundle still validates.
assertions: tables/returns.md exists with type, title and one-sentence description
resource field identifies the acme.sales.returns BigQuery table
Schema lists all four columns with their types
Body links to the orders concept for the order_id foreign key
sources has an entry for https://wiki.acme/data/returns with an id that is cited by a keyed footnote
generated.by is an agent actor (not human:) with an ISO datetime with offset
No fabricated `verified` entry on the new concept
tables/index.md lists the new returns concept
log.md has a 2026-09-27 entry at the top mentioning returns
Bundle validates with 0 errors and 0 warnings (okf.py validate)
No existing concept files other than index.md/log.md were modified (neighbouring edits suggested, not made)
viz.html was not hand-edited, and the response tells the user it is now out of date

evals.prompt: Here's an old OKF v0.1 doc (income-statement.md). Migrate it to v0.2 properly, splitting out the SQL the way the spec wants.
evals.expected_output: A narrative Metric concept linking to two Attested Computation concepts (revenue on bigquery, gross profit), each with runtime, parameters, computation block, sources with ids and keyed footnotes, generated instead of timestamp; no # Citations; validates clean.
assertions: Narrative Metric concept no longer has `timestamp` and has `generated: {by, at}`
Narrative concept has no `# Citations` section
At least two `type: Attested Computation` concepts exist (revenue and gross profit)
Each Attested Computation has runtime, parameters, and a computation (body block or computation: file)
SQL placeholders are converted to runtime parameter binding (no `<year>`/`<segment>` left)
Metric concept links to both computation concepts
All three wiki URLs are preserved as sources entries with ids cited by keyed footnotes
No fabricated human `verified` entries
Bundle validates with 0 errors and 0 warnings (okf.py validate)
Gross-profit computation keeps the source's engine: runtime bigquery and no dbt ref()/var() syntax
Every computation's executor.resource and attester.resource exist in the bundle
The attester is Python that compiles and actually rejects a tampered receipt (checked by reading it)
